title: WPMS/1444/2012 of CHATAR SINGH Vs MADAN SINGH AND ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.1444 of 2010 (M/S)

Sri Chatar Singh S/o Sri Kashiram
R/o Village Kyarkuli Bhatta
Mussoorie Road, Dehradun
 ......Petitioner
Versus
Sri Madan Singh S/o Sri Sher Singh R/o Village Kyarkuli Bhatta,
Mussoorie Road, Dehradun and seven others.
 .......Respondents
Hon'ble B.S.Verma, J.
 Sri Jitendra Chaudhary, Advocate present for the
petitioner.
 Sri A. Rab, Senior Advocate assisted by Sri Amish
Tiwari, Advocate present for the respondents.
 Heard.
 By means of this writ petition, petitioner has sought
following relief :-
i. Set-aside/quash the impugned ex-party order dated
 06.07.2012 (Annexure-12) passed by the Board of
 Revenue in Revenue Revision No.11/2011-12 " Govind
 Singh & others Vs. Chatar Singh" and further be pleased
 to quash entire proceedings of aforesaid Revenue
 Revision No.11/2011-12 as not maintainable.
ii. Further it is prayed that a direction may also be issued
to the respondents that they shall not raise any further
construction on the spot nor create third party interest
in the property in dispute in future during pendency of
the demarcation proceedings before the Assistant
Collector First Class/SDM, Dehradun.
iii. Or pass any other order writ or direction which this
Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the
circumstances of the case.
iv. Award the cost of the writ petition.

2
 Briefly stated the facts giving rise to this writ petition are
that petitioner Chatar Singh filed an application under section 41 of
U.P. of Land Revenue Act, 1901 for demarcation of the Land before
the Assistant Collector Ist Class/Deputy Collector, Sadar, Dehradun.
The said application is pending for final disposal. On the basis of
report received from Survey Naib Tehsildar, Assistant Collector
passed an interim order on 16.06.2012 directing the parties not to
make any construction, digging or change the nature of the land or
sell the land in question till further orders measurement of the Land
is done.
 Aggrieved by the aforesaid order, Revision was preferred
by the respondents before Board of Revenue, Uttarakhand,
Dehradun for setting aside the order dated 16.06.2012. On
26.06.2012 Board of Revenue, Dehradun stayed the operation of
order dated 16.06.2012 and the record was summoned from the
court below and fix 10.07.2012 in revision for hearing. Thereafter,
an application was moved by the petitioner Chatar Singh for setting
aside the order dated 26.06.2012 till the completion of demarcation
of Land in question. After hearing the petitioner Chatar Singh, on
the said application, Board of Revenue passed an order on
28.06.2012 directing the parties to maintain status-quo without
giving opportunity of hearing to the revisionist/respondent.
Thereafter, another application was moved on 02.07.2012 by the
revisionist with the prayer to recall the order to maintain status-quo
passed on 28.06.2011 on the ground that plot No.2994/1 which the
petitioner claims his own plot belongs to the revisionist is plot
No.2988 as per report of the Revenue Inspector. Therefore,
considering this aspect, the order dated 28.06.2012 was recalled on
06.07.2012. Aggrieved by the said order, petitioner/opposite party
in revision has preferred this writ petition for quashing the
impugned order dated 06.07.2012 passed by the Board of Revenue
in Revenue Revision No.11/2011-12 "Govind Singh & others Vs.
Chatar Singh".

3
 It is pertinent to mention here that proceedings under
section 41 of U.P. Land Revenue Act are summary in nature. Under
Section 41 of the Act, Assistant Collector can direct to handover the
possession of the land in question to the applicant if any other
tenure holder is found in possession of his land after due enquiry.
But so far as to grant the injunction is concerned, no such power has
been given to the Assistant Collector to grant the injunction against
any of the tenure holder. So far as the provisions of the C.P.C.
applicable to the proceeding of U.P. Land Revenue Act have been
mentioned in Appendix First of Revenue Court manual, which
indicates, that provisions of Order 39 Rule 1 & 2 C.P.C. has not been
made applicable to the proceeding of Land Revenue Act.
 Therefore, prima facie, order passed by Assistant
Collector on 16.06.2012 directing the parties not to make any
construction or change the nature of the land or sell the land in
question is without jurisdiction. The Civil Court or the Assistant
Collector while exercising the power under section 229-B of Z.A. &
L.R. Act in regular suit when application has been moved under
section 229-D of the Act. Under Section 41 of U.P. Land Revenue
Act, the Assistant Collector does not have such power to grant
interim reliefs.
 Therefore, I find no error in the order of learned
Commissioner whereby impugned order of status quo was recalled
and order assailed in revision was stayed. The writ petition is
dismissed being devoid of merit. Learned Board of Revenue,
Dehradun is directed to decide the revision preferably within a
period of eight weeks from the date of production of certified copy of
this order expeditiously as far as possible.
 (B.S.Verma, J.)
 08.08.2012
JKJ
